business_review.text: A single virtual assistant can be assigned to multiple workflow steps in the visual editor without duplication.
business_review.notes: shouldReuseActorId returns true for any referencing state; generateActorID is never called for shared assistant states.

business_review.text: Editing any step referencing a shared assistant updates that assistant in-place; no duplicate is created.
business_review.notes: All referencing states get canReuseId=true, preserving the same assistantId on every save.

business_review.text: The assistant-to-state reference relationship is preserved after any UI modification.
business_review.notes: assistant_id in each state is carried through unchanged since the existing ID is always reused.

business_review.text: Workflows imported via YAML with shared assistants are handled correctly by the UI.
business_review.notes: YAML import populates config.states with original assistant_id values; subsequent UI edits hit the fixed code path.

business_review.text: Tool and custom-node actor sharing behavior is unchanged.
business_review.notes: Tool and CustomNode fall through to the unchanged exclusive-ownership guard. Existing regression tests confirm.

standards_review.notes: Message 'EPMCDME-10583: Allow shared assistant actors to be updated in-place on step edit' matches the required EPMCDME-NNNN: Capital sentence pattern.
No new `any` introductions; tsc --noEmit passed in pre-commit lint-staged.
Three new test cases added covering multi-reference shared assistant scenarios. Existing Tool/CustomNode multi-reference tests unchanged and passing.

findings.problem: The JSDoc comment for shouldReuseActorId describes the old symmetric contract ('Returns true if the actor is used by only one node (the current one)'; 'Returns false if the actor is used by multiple nodes or doesn't exist'). This is now incorrect for ActorTypes.Assistant — the function returns true for a shared assistant as long as the current state is among the referencers.
findings.impact: Any developer reading the JSDoc will apply the wrong mental model (exclusive-ownership semantics) when the actual behaviour for Assistant actors is shared-ownership semantics. This will lead to incorrect usage or suppression of the function in future changes.
findings.recommendation: Update the JSDoc to describe the asymmetric contract: for Tool and CustomNode, returns true only when the current state is the sole referencer; for Assistant, returns true whenever the current state is any referencer. Update the @returns tag to match.

rationale: All 5 acceptance criteria pass. One major finding: the JSDoc for shouldReuseActorId describes the old exclusive-ownership contract and is now misleading for the Assistant case. Fix is a documentation-only change. Deferred: EC-002 (silent shared-actor mutation) is the ticket's intended behaviour per explicit user requirement ('no warning, silent save'). EC-003 (useEffect reset for co-open panels) is a pre-existing concern not introduced by this diff; panel lifecycle in the visual editor makes simultaneous editing of two panels unlikely. Dismissed: blind-lens findings on test setup pedantry, non-Assistant fallthrough coverage, and multi-true returns — none are real defects.
